who_for: A smartwatch is worth it if you want notifications on your wrist, fitness and health tracking, or both. Your phone decides a lot. Apple Watches only work with iPhones, while Samsung, Pixel, and Garmin watches work best with Android or across both.
If you mostly want fitness tracking and long battery life, a fitness-focused watch or band can be a better and cheaper choice than a full smartwatch.

how_we_picked.label: Phone compatibility
how_we_picked.text: We grouped picks by which phones they work with, since that limits your choices before anything else.

how_we_picked.label: Health and fitness tracking
how_we_picked.text: We compared heart rate, GPS accuracy, sleep tracking, and health features like ECG, based on expert testing and owner feedback.

how_we_picked.label: Battery life
how_we_picked.text: We weighed realistic battery life with typical use, from about a day for some smartwatches to more than a week for fitness watches.

how_we_picked.label: Display and comfort
how_we_picked.text: A bright, readable screen and a comfortable fit matter for something you wear all day.

how_we_picked.label: Apps and features
how_we_picked.text: We looked at app support, payments, and cellular options for each platform.
